key_insights: Test-optional colleges let applicants choose whether to include SAT/ACT scores in their application.
If scores are strong and above a target school's average, submitting them can strengthen the application.
If scores are below the typical range for target schools or don't reflect true ability, it may be better to withhold them and lean on GPA, coursework, and recommendations instead.
Some test-optional schools still require standardized English proficiency tests for international applicants even when SAT/ACT is optional.
Notes that some colleges have recently reversed course and gone back to requiring or recommending test scores after being test-optional, so policies should be checked per school and per year.
notable_or_distinctive: Generic advice; the only slightly distinctive point is the reminder that international applicants may still need English proficiency tests even at test-optional schools, and that some schools have reversed test-optional policies.
reliability_notes: No named speaker or credentials given; content is generic and could describe any test-optional situation without citing specific colleges, so treat as general orientation rather than authoritative guidance; also dated quickly given fast-changing testing policies.
